test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. a man in a maroon colour flannel shirt

Q. rounded a corner and walked into the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky

R. which had been purchased for purposes of decoration

S. and made principally by some Jewish women on the East side of New York
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence parts need to be arranged to form a meaningful sentence.

• Option 2 'PRSQ' is the correct arrangement because it logically sequences the sentence.

• Starting with 'P' introduces the subject, 'a man in a maroon colour flannel shirt'.

• 'R' logically follows as it describes the shirt 'which had been purchased for purposes of decoration', adding detail to the subject introduced in 'P'.

• 'S' cannot directly follow 'P' as it introduces an unrelated detail that breaks the logical flow of the sentence.

• 'Q' correctly concludes the sentence by placing the man 'in the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky', following the introduction and description of the shirt.

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *'a man in a maroon colour flannel shirt which had been purchased for purposes of decoration rounded a corner and walked into the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky'*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Option 1 'PRQS' incorrectly places 'S' at the end, which breaks the logical flow of the sentence by introducing an unrelated detail after concluding the action.

• Option 3 'PSRQ' incorrectly starts with detail about the shirt's creation before introducing the shirt or the subject wearing it, creating confusion.

• Option 4 'PQRS' places 'S' immediately after 'P', which disrupts the logical description and action sequence regarding the man and his shirt.
